title: Site ground r3: A cloud volume carved by one negative pseudo-Gaussian sphere, a sun at the hollow's bottom lights the walls and orbits, the camera follows low inside; pre-pass, camera-aware TAA
first: Map: F:/Projects/CultLib/docs/cultmath-interval-ground-cut.md, 'Pass 3' (the void scene, the composed bound, the pre-pass, the budget), then 'The shader design' for what pass 3 does not restate (sampled wash, palette input, pausing, contrast). Rulings in force: cultmath-tapes:ruling:operator-ground-void-brush (the scene), operator-tile-amortized-march (the march), site-masthead:ruling:operator-chromeless-column; wash-home-only's authority map. Re-pin base to main after wash-home-only lands. Stardust and DoF stay the next cut; leave the named composite slot. r2's token, readback, controller, vendoring, parity and fallback items stand unless this revision names them.

The original, read once (Aetheria at e6181c11, 2021-03-13, Assets/Scenes/Main Menu.unity; Prefabs/RPG/Planets/Sun.prefab; Materials/Brushes/Gravity Well.mat, Main Menu Sun Fog Tint.mat, Main Menu Ambient Fog Tint.mat, Sector Boundary Fog.mat; Materials/Fog Marching Main Menu.mat; Shaders/Raymarching/VolumeRender.shader at that commit; Shaders/Brushes/PowerBrush.shader). What survives, in the original's units: the brush is PowerBrush (1 - x^2)^16 with depth 40 over radius 256 (half depth at r = 52, pseudo-Gaussian sigma about 45), the sun's own gravity-well child; a wide boundary bowl (depth 75, power 0.25, radius 1500) is flat across the scene and acts as a constant 75; floor offset -16.46, floor blend 39.6, so the fog top is at y = -91 outside the void and dips to -131 at the sun; the sun sphere (radius 12.5) sits at y = -130, the bottom of the void.

What survives (continued): the sun is a child of 'Center', which rotates 5 degrees per second about y (72 s period), at orbit radius 175; the camera is a Cinemachine vcam following the sun (framing transposer, distance 150, damping 10, handheld noise amplitude 1 at frequency 0.25) and looking at 'Look Target' (0, -130, 0), the orbit centre at the sun's depth; the saved camera sits at y = -27, 64 above the fog top. The lighting was authored, not marched: the sun's 'Fog Tint' brush (1 - x^2)^3, depth 2, radius 128, colour (1, 0.4, 0.1) orange, painted into the tint map, times a scene-wide ambient tint (0.18, 0.59, 1) blue, depth 0.01. Stardust: 256^2 particles, spacing 2, floor -60, ceiling 0, height exponent 800 / (ceiling + wellDepth) so particles climb higher where the well is deeper (the void fills with stardust). Noise: strength 150, frequency 0.01, safety 50. Not surviving: the 2021 d() details, the tint map's runtime contents, the video.

The field (ruling operator-void-true-cavity: a spherical hollow inside a cloud volume that surrounds it on every side, not the 2021 bowl). Units are the original's. Outer volume: an unbounded uniform fill, chosen over a shell because every ray then ends in a wall and the march terminates by opacity, never by a far plane; Z1 = |camera - c_v| + Rc + 6/K (614 at the shipped point) bounds the pre-pass range and is past opacity for every ray, so the analytic body step below always terminates. The carve is the pseudo-Gaussian brush g(d) = (1 - (d / Rc)^2)^e, d = |p - c_v|, density = K max(0, 1 - CARVE g(d')), authored by two knobs: the hollow radius Rh (density exactly 0 inside; Rh = Rc sqrt(1 - CARVE^(-1/e))) and the ramp width S (density full at Rh + S; set by the exponent: e = 4 gives S = 1.3 Rh, e = 0.25 gives S = 0.12 Rh).

Shipped (Q9 in the map, option (a) pending the operator): Rh = 198, S = 50, so Rc = Rh + S = 248 and e = -ln CARVE / ln(1 - (Rh / Rc)^2) = 0.40; CARVE = 1.5, K = 1/30: a wall is opaque within about 150 units of full density. The ramp and the noise fade band are both S wide; nothing void-shaped is authored twice (interval-ops r3, finding shipped-void-two-scenes). Noise displaces the wall only: fade(d) = smoothstep(Rh - S, Rh, d), d' = d + A fade(d) n(warp(p)), A = 20, F0 = 0.01.

Scene motion. The sun orbits the origin at radius 175 in xz with period 72 s (5 degrees per second, the original's Center pivot). The cavity centre is c_v = sun + (0, Rh - 12.5, 0): the sun sphere (radius 12.5) rests on the hollow's bottom and the hollow moves with it. The camera follows the sun 120 behind it along the orbit's tangent and 45 above it, so it sits 186 from c_v, 12 inside the hollow (the handheld drift is 2 units, two low-frequency snoise on time), low in the cavity, looking at the sun's position plus (0, 60, 0) so the lit lower wall and the dark upper wall share the frame. The 2021 follow distance 150 and height 25 do not fit a hollow a camera can stand in; 120 and 45 are the re-derivation, and the report says so. worldAt(t) in ground.js is the one owner of sun, cavity and camera, uploaded as uniforms; the shaders never integrate motion.

The flow field, authored around the void: flow(xz) = SWIRL * tangent(xz - sun.xz) * (1 - (r / Rw)^2)^2 + GLOBAL * (snoise(xz Ff + o1), snoise(xz Ff + o2)) (the swirl is largest mid-slope and zero at the rim and the centre; the global term is r2's). The flow texture is a world-space window of side 4 Rw centred on the sun, quarter of the canvas resolution, re-rendered every frame; warp, hue, motion vectors and (next cut) the stardust read it, so D4 holds with a moving scene. D = FLOW_MAX * PERIOD / 2 as before, with FLOW_MAX the authored maximum of the swirl plus the global amplitude.

The march (tile pre-pass, interval-ops r2's design). Pre-pass at W/8 x H/8: per tile, the loop over the slab's cell ranges (uniform cells, StepDense = min(10, S / 4) = 10, 62 cells to Z1 = 614 along +view depth; the mask has 96 bits): the envelope probe first (exact box: y and xz ranges by cultmath_iv_mul of the depth and slope intervals, d's interval is the box's least and greatest distance to c_v, exact; g, fade and the carve are monotone in it), then the noise ball (cultmath_iv_frustum_ball with D, cultmath_iv_snoise_ball) only when fade.hi > 0 and L r F0 leaves room to prove anything; writes the 96-bit mask of cells not proven empty to an RGBA32UI texel's first three words, and in the fourth word the body-start cell: the first cell whose own bound is a positive point and whose slice to Z1 is one too (the envelope with the free noise interval proves density exactly K for the rest of the range), 0xFFFFFFFF when none (interval-ops r3, ruling operator-analytic-wall-body).

(March, continued.) Main pass: texelFetch the mask, then march the unmasked range with the footprint step Delta(z) and the octave weights (next item), the per-frame sample count capped by the budget S_budget and the start jittered so TAA completes what one frame does not; masked cells are skipped exactly; at the body-start cell take one analytic Beer-Lambert step, T *= exp(-K (Z1 - z) |dir|) with K the field's pointwise envelope value there (no probe in the main pass), and stop; integrate transmittance and the depth-weighted mean distance, apply the light. Every tile's interior cells retire in a few envelope probes and its wall cells are marked; there are no sky tiles. Behind a fully transmissive pixel the resolve shows --gamecult-nebula-base; by construction only an unfinished ray (budget exhausted before the wall, measured, must be under 1%) reaches it.

Footprint LOD (the operator's challenge, map 'Footprint LOD'): theta_px = 2 tan(fov/2) / H; the footprint at distance z is z theta_px. Step: Delta(z) = max(k z theta_px, min(S / 4, lambda_fine(z) / 2)), k = 4: never finer than four footprints, otherwise the finer of the two content limits (four samples across the ramp, two per wavelength of the finest live octave). Octaves: octave i of wavelength lambda_i carries weight w_i(z) = 1 - smoothstep(lambda_i / (2m), lambda_i / m, z theta_px), m = 4: one smooth blend per octave, no popping; TAA hides per-frame sparsity. The weights are part of the field, so the bound encloses the truncated field exactly: the noise interval over a slice is the sum over octaves of iv_mul([w_i(z1), w_i(z0)], iv_snoise_ball(c F_i, r F_i)), w_i monotone in z. At the shipped parameters (wavelengths 100 and 25, z <= 2 Rc) every weight is 1 in the frustum and the content limits set the step; the footprint bites when S < 4 k z theta_px.

Where the scene sits and what to turn (Imagination's model, scratchpad cavity_model.py; the test and the browser confirm): interval-ops r2 measured the shipped point at 16.45 LOD steps and 26.6 snoise per pixel against 36.3 fixed steps (2.21x); r3's analytic body is predicted to bring the steps to about 12.5 (2.6-3.3x), snoise unchanged; the wall's step is set by S / 4 and the detail half-wavelength, not by distance; the browser confirms or refutes. Cheaper without losing the mood, in order: (1) a lower per-frame S_budget, which LOD and the mask make nearly lossless (S_budget = 4 converges in about three frames at the walls); (2) a thinner ramp S (S = 10 is 3.2x on cost but reads as a surface; 25-50 keeps the fog); (3) a longer detail wavelength or no detail octave near the far wall (the 12.5-unit half-wavelength is the floor for S >= 50); (4) a larger hollow (Rh = 1000: 2.5x) costs nothing per pixel and changes the composition. Camera offset barely matters at these scales.

Lighting, the cheapest version that keeps it moody (the original's own mechanism, made 3D): at each sample, light = SUN_COLOUR * (1 - (d / Rl)^2)^3 for d = |p - sun| < Rl, Rl = Rh = 198 (the original's 128 scaled with the hollow), plus AMBIENT * ambientTint; colour = density * (light + ambient) * hue(flow). No light march: zero extra snoise, one length and one pow per sample. The lower wall within Rl of the sun glows and the upper wall stays dark because the pulse is zero beyond Rl, which is the moody split; the sun inside the hollow is occluded by nothing, so the sun itself is a small additive disc drawn in the resolve at its projected position, occluded by the accumulated transmittance along its ray. Not in this cut, measured before it is ever added: one envelope-only transmittance sample toward the sun per primary sample (self-shadowing by the bowl's geometry), about +25% march cost; it is desktop-only if ever.

TAA with a moving camera. ground.js uploads this frame's and the previous frame's view-projection. For each pixel the resolve reconstructs the world point at the march's depth-weighted mean distance (written by the main pass into a second history channel, R16F), moves it back by the field motion (p + flow(p) * dt: the pattern moves at -flow), projects it with the previous VP and fetches history at that uv. The same 3x3 min/max clamp, alpha = max(1/frames, 1/32), out-of-bounds alpha 1; history reset on resize, first frame and budget step. Transmittance, colour and the depth channel are all reprojected by the one motion vector. ?ground=debug-mv shows |mv| with the camera moving and the flow frozen, and with the flow moving and the camera frozen, so both terms are seen separately.

Stardust distribution and the sun disc are the next cut (site-stardust), authored to the void: particles spawned in the bowl's volume with the original's height rule (more headroom where the well is deeper), lit by the same pulse, moving with the swirl. This cut leaves the composite slot and the depth history they need.

Fit with the tokens. Inputs: --gamecult-nebula-0 (orange 255 138 42) is SUN_COLOUR; --gamecult-nebula-2 (sky 89 183 255) is the ambient tint; --gamecult-nebula-1 (violet 109 96 255) is the cloud hue's second pole; --gamecult-nebula-base the sky. Outputs from the 8x8 readback as r2, with one change: --gamecult-light-0-at is written from the sun's projected screen position (quantised to 1%, at most 2 Hz), so the CSS wash's main light follows the sun while the shader runs; --gamecult-light-0 and -a come from the texel there; lights 1 and 2 keep their seed positions and sample their colours. When the canvas is absent the seeds paint a still of the same composition (the seed light-0-at is the sun's mean screen position).

Prove in the browser pane, in addition to r2's list: with ?ground=debug the pre-pass's mean probes per tile and the fraction of cells masked, and the mean snoise per pixel and the fraction of samples placed in the wall ramp against a dense-reference frame (?ground=dense: no pre-pass, S samples over the whole slab; the two converged frames' mean luminance agree within 1/255; the masked frame's per-frame variance at the walls is lower, printed); the camera reprojection test above; the orbit (after 36 s the sun's screen position has moved half an orbit and the TAA shows no smear at the walls); the contrast clamp with the lit cavity (max luminance <= 0.035 still holds; the sun disc is exempt only inside its own radius, which the clamp test masks and reports).

authority_map.owner: The shader owns the ground. ground.js owns worldAt(t) (sun, void, camera), the flow texture, the pre-pass mask, the march, the TAA, the readback and the sampled tokens; custom.scss owns the four nebula inputs, --gamecult-wash and the seeds; CultLib owns every noise and interval function; the composed bound in prepass.frag.glsl is built from cultmath_iv_* only.
inputs: the four nebula tokens and --gamecult-wash (computed on body)
prefers-reduced-motion, visibilityState, canvas size, devicePixelRatio, elapsed time
measured GPU frame time (timer query, fence, or rAF cadence)
the shader's own 8x8 readback and the sun's projected position
the vendored CultMath.glsl at its pinned CultLib commit
outputs: one opaque moving canvas under the page, luminance <= 0.035 outside the sun disc
the fifteen ground tokens and --gamecult-ground-mean on :root inline, at most 2 Hz; light-0-at follows the sun
debug, dense-reference and parity readbacks (console, flag only)
derived_state: sun, void and camera positions are derived from time by worldAt(t); nothing integrates motion frame to frame
the tile mask is derived each frame from that frame's camera and the field; it is never carried across frames
the flow texture is the one owner of motion: warp, hue, motion vectors and the stardust read it
the TAA history (colour, transmittance, depth) is a cache reprojected by camera and flow; reset on resize, first frame and budget step
the ground tokens are derived from the readback while the shader runs; the seeds are the fallback; the shader never reads them
S and dpr are derived from measurement within the session; the sessionStorage token set is a cache
forbidden_writers: no colour, alpha, position or radius literal in ground.js or any GLSL file; the scene's dimensions (H0, Dw, Rw, F, S, Rl, orbit radius, period, camera offset) are named constants in one place in ground.js, uploaded as uniforms
no sample placed in a masked cell; no probe in the main pass; no early-out of the pre-pass on transmittance
no light march in this cut; the light is the analytic pulse
no read of the ground output tokens by the shader or ground.js except the seed read before the first readback
no userAgent, platform or maxTouchPoints; no class or attribute set on body or html; no second wash token; no second flow evaluation; no noise or interval function defined in the site's GLSL
no synchronous readPixels to client memory; one requestAnimationFrame scheduler; localStorage never
shared_paths: every page paints one canvas and one token set; the ritual essays differ only in seeds and inputs
slow device, hidden tab, reduced motion, missing WebGL2 and missing half-float all pass through the one controller
the 8x8 readback and the sun projection are the only paths from the shader to CSS
the pre-pass and the main pass read the same uniforms from the same worldAt(t); the dense-reference mode differs only by skipping the mask
authority_map.deletion_line: As r2: the ritual block's own background and the body literals go in the same commit the tokens are declared. Nothing else in the engine or content changes. Against pass 2's design this revision removes the static camera and the everywhere-clouds field; it adds one pre-pass, one mask texture, one depth history channel and the scene function.
